subject: Suspicious sessions observed — ask re: log hold and export
messages:
From: Marco Diaz <marco.d@finserveco.com>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.example.com
Cc: ops@finserveco.com
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Suspicious sessions observed — need retention/export guidance

Hi Camila,

We noticed a cluster of anomalous sessions yesterday that accessed a small set of sensitive endpoints. Security flagged ~120 session IDs and we've attached a CSV with the IDs and timestamps. Can Redwood put a legal/forensic hold on the relevant logs while we investigate? Two quick questions: 1) how long can you retain request logs for a customer hold, and 2) what evidence/export formats can you provide (full request/response, headers-only, redacted)?

We need this info to brief our compliance team and to determine whether to open a regulatory notification. Happy to hop on a short call if helpful.

Thanks,
Marco Diaz
Sr. Ops Engineer — FinServeCo
attachments: session-ids.csv (csv), suspicious-traffic-snippet.txt (text)
From: camila_reyes@redwood.example.com
To: Marco Diaz <marco.d@finserveco.com>
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.example.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 09:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Suspicious sessions observed — need retention/export guidance

Hi Marco — thanks for the heads up and for the CSV.

Short answer: we can place an immediate retention hold and produce exports, but we need a couple of clarifications to scope the work and avoid unnecessary retention of unrelated data:
- Time window: what UTC start/end should we hold? (example: 2028-03-14T22:00Z to 2028-03-15T03:00Z)
- Data types: do you need full request/response bodies, or headers/metadata only? Full bodies increase export complexity and may include PII.
- Is this a legal hold requested by counsel, or an operational incident response? If legal, please route through the authorized contact (legal@finserveco.com).

Proposed immediate actions from Redwood:
1) Snapshot inbound/outbound request logs for the session IDs you provided and place a 90-day hold on the snapshot (can be extended).
2) Generate a headers+metadata export by default; full bodies are available on request with confirmation of scope and retention.
3) Preserve the current KV cache snapshots for the affected model variants (if applicable) — will need to coordinate with infra.

Evelyn (security) and Karthik (incidents) are looped for chain-of-custody and export mechanics. If you confirm the time window and desired export level we can start the snapshot within the hour.

- Camila
Camila Reyes
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
From: evelyn_hart@redwood.example.com
To: camila_reyes@redwood.example.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com
Cc: Marco Diaz <marco.d@finserveco.com>, ops@finserveco.com
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Suspicious sessions observed — need retention/export guidance

On Thu, Mar 15, 2028 at 09:37 AM camila_reyes@redwood.example.com wrote:
> Proposed immediate actions from Redwood:
> 1) Snapshot inbound/outbound request logs for the session IDs you provided and place a 90-day hold on the snapshot (can be extended).
> 2) Generate a headers+metadata export by default; full bodies are available on request with confirmation of scope and retention.

Hi all — confirming we can perform the snapshot and lock it down. A few operational notes from Sec/Ops:
- Chain of custody: we'll create a sealed export bundle (gzip) with a manifest and SHA256 checksums. The bundle will be stored in a read-only bucket under a retention hold.
- Access: exports are accessible only to authorized contacts listed in FinServeCo's security contact list + Redwood incident responders; please confirm the FinServeCo approvers for retrieval.
- Redaction: for full-body exports, we can run a PII redaction pass but need an approved PII schema from your side to avoid removing data that might be evidence.
- Timeline: snapshot and manifest creation estimated ~2 hours from approval for the 3-hour window; full-body export could take additional 4–6 hours depending on size.

If Marco confirms the exact window and that this is an operational hold (not a legal hold), Karthik will kick the snapshot and I'll own the chain-of-custody artifacts.

—Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Senior Security Engineer — Redwood Inference

Time window (UTC): 2028-03-14T23:30:00Z to 2028-03-15T02:45:00Z
Export level: headers+metadata first. If analysis requires, we'll request full bodies (we'll provide PII schema).
Hold type: operational incident response (not legal).
Approvers for retrieval: Marco Diaz (marco.d@finserveco.com), Priya Shah (pri.shah@finserveco.com) — both on ops@finserveco.com distribution.

Please proceed with the snapshot and upload the sealed bundle link when ready. We may schedule a 20-minute call after you upload to walk through the manifest.

—Marco
